title: AttestationStatusV1
description: Revocation and supersession status for a Spend Attestation at a point in time — the native, non-VC-specific counterpart to the two BitstringStatusListEntry purposes this repository already defines for the W3C credential binding. Unreleased draft schema (object-model artifact, board step OM4).
$comment: Derived from README.md#core-objects ("AttestationStatus | Trust | Revocation and supersession."); 01-core/verification-state.md, which defines the attestation head classes this schema's `statusBasis` enum reuses verbatim ('HARD_VERIFIED, CORRECTED, and INVALIDATED are attestation head classes' / 'INVALIDATED is terminal for spend truth'); 02-proof-lifecycle/correction-and-revocation.md, which states that v1 defines no REVOKED event or state ('The requested lifecycle term revoked maps to later invalidating/correction semantics only when a future protocol version defines a revocation event; v1 does not silently invent one') and that SPEND_CORRECTED supersedes by moving the head rather than retroactively editing it; and 03-portability/w3c-vc-2.0-binding.md, which fixes exactly two status purposes -- 'revocation' and 'refresh' (not the full upstream W3C purpose set; no 'suspension') -- states both are required and ordered per credential, that a set bit is irreversible, and that 'A CORRECTED head is a superseding claim and MUST NOT be marked revoked only because a later head exists.' `statusPurpose`'s enum literally matches 07-conformance/profiles/w3c-vc-2.0-spend-attestation-v1/protocol/schemas/w3c_bitstring_status_list_credential_v1.schema.json's `statusPurpose` enum. `reason` mirrors the required `reason` field on bindings/nats/crinkl-platform/v1/schemas/event.spend_invalidated.schema.json's payload. This schema intentionally does not invent a REVOKED status-basis value; only the three attestation head classes the repository already names are exposed. RELATIONSHIP TO THE W3C BITSTRING STATUS LIST CREDENTIAL: this artifact is the protocol-level status object and does NOT supersede, replace, or subsume the W3C-profile serialization of status, `07-conformance/profiles/w3c-vc-2.0-spend-attestation-v1/protocol/schemas/w3c_bitstring_status_list_credential_v1.schema.json` (a `BitstringStatusListCredential`/`BitstringStatusList` VC carrying an `encodedList` bitstring, referenced from a `SpendAttestationCredential` via `BitstringStatusListEntry`). That credential remains the W3C-profile-internal, VC-wrapped, bit-indexed serialization used when a Spend Attestation is presented as a W3C credential; this schema is the native, non-VC record of the same `statusPurpose` vocabulary (`revocation`/`refresh`) for any Spend Attestation regardless of serialization. This schema references, and does not replace, the W3C artifact's status semantics.

spendId.description: Identifies the spend stream this status describes (01-core/spend-event.md).

statusBasis.description: The attestation head class this status reflects. These are the only three attestation head classes this repository defines (01-core/verification-state.md); no REVOKED basis exists in v1 (02-proof-lifecycle/correction-and-revocation.md).

statusPurpose.description: Matches the exact two status-list purposes this repository defines for the W3C binding; not the full upstream W3C purpose set (03-portability/w3c-vc-2.0-binding.md).

set.description: Whether the bit for this purpose is set. Irreversible once true: a set-to-clear transition is invalid (03-portability/w3c-vc-2.0-binding.md).

supersededByRef.description: Content address of the superseding artifact when statusBasis is CORRECTED. A CORRECTED head MUST NOT set the revocation purpose solely because a later head exists (03-portability/w3c-vc-2.0-binding.md); use this field together with a refresh-purpose entry instead. null otherwise.

reason.description: Present when statusBasis is INVALIDATED, mirroring the required `reason` field on the SPEND_INVALIDATED event payload. null otherwise.

asOf.description: When this status determination was made.
